acceptance_cases.exercise: loop_entry
acceptance_cases.expected_outcome: For state-field loop_entry, preserve documented meaning, defaults, invalid/missing-value behavior and lifecycle rules: | `loop_entry` | object? | PRD 00282: the Phase 0 (`enter()`) result the loop ran in-process before launching a build session, or before consuming a `park-requested` marker — `Loop._pre_enter`. Shape: `{"entered_by": "loop", "prd": string, "result": object}`, where `result` is the same dict `autopilot enter` would otherwise print (its `warnings` key already popped and sent to the loop's own stderr). The session brief's `## Entry` section mirrors `result`'s `prd`/`catchup`/`design`/`stop`. The next `autopilot enter` call (inside the launched session) reads this FIRST: a `loop_entry.prd` matching `state.prd`, with no `--prd` given, replays `result` as that call's one JSON line and deletes `loop_entry` without re-running `enter()` — so a selection produces exactly one resume row. A `loop_entry` whose `prd` no longer matches (stale — state moved on since the loop wrote it) is dropped and `enter()` runs normally. Absent when `enter()` raised `state.StateError`, when the state write failed (one stderr line, logged, no `loop_entry`), or in a manual/interactive session (which never runs `_pre_enter`). Also cleared by Phase 9 step 10 on PRD-to-PRD reset, as defense-in-depth against a crash between the loop's write and the launched session's consume. |

acceptance_cases.exercise: tasks[].attempts
acceptance_cases.expected_outcome: For state-field tasks[].attempts, preserve documented meaning, defaults, invalid/missing-value behavior and lifecycle rules: | `tasks[].attempts` | object[]? | Per-task execution log: `{"attempt": int, "model": string, "outcome": "completed"\|"aborted"\|"review_flagged"\|"rework_failed"\|"escalated", "review_cycle": int\|null, "cause": string\|null, "implementor": "claude"\|"gemini"\|"qwen"\|"codex"\|"orchestrator", "preflight_outcome": "healthy"\|"pi_missing"\|"endpoint_unreachable"\|"model_id_missing"\|"completion_failed"\|null, "pipeline"?: "minimal"\|"lean"\|"full", "self_deslop"?: string, "escalation_reason"?: "gate_failure"\|"review_flag"\|"fable_rescue", "escalated_from"?: "qwen"\|"haiku"\|"sonnet"\|"opus"\|"codex", "diagnosis"?: "spec_gap"\|"solid_spec", "repair_used"?: true, "breaker_skipped"?: true, "qwen_gate_failed"?: true, "qwen_excluded_reason"?: "files"\|"memory_pressure"\|"memory_probe_failed", "codex_no_edit"?: true, "codex_no_edit_probe_exit"?: int, "micro_lane"?: "overrun", "reflow"?: string, "review"?: string, "style_gate"?: string, "devon"?: "skipped:prose"\|"exploit_fixed"\|null, "devon_exploit"?: string, "devon_weak_points"?: int, "devon_in_contract"?: string[], "split_hygiene"?: string, "verification"?: string}`. Records each Work pass on the task. Appended by `/autopilot:work` at task exit (success or abort). The `implementor` field reflects what actually dispatched (NOT what step 3's routing table initially picked — a qwen pick that fell back to Claude on preflight failure records `"claude"`). The `preflight_outcome` field is set only for attempts on qwen-eligible tasks (effective eligibility after runtime write-set reconciliation); for non-qwen-eligible attempts (UI tasks, `opus`-tier tasks, backend tasks where `qwen_eligible` is `false` or absent) it is `null`. A qwen-eligible attempt that the breaker (row 3) or the memory-pressure gate (row 4) rerouted also records `null`, because the probe never ran. The `pipeline` field records the tier-gated pipeline depth the attempt ran — `"minimal"`/`"lean"`/`"full"` for `haiku`/`sonnet`/`opus`, `"full"` for `fable`, and `"solo"` for a task the solo lane's session edited itself (`references/lane-solo.md`, PRD 00205; always paired with `implementor: "orchestrator"`) (the rescue rung runs the deepest pipeline, like `opus`; absent/legacy `model` is treated as `sonnet` → `"lean"`), written at every task exit (PRD 00044) — the `?` in the signature marks read-side tolerance for pre-00044 rows only; new writes always include `pipeline`. **Cardinality (PRD 00065):** today `/autopilot:work` appends exactly one entry per task at exit. Under in-loop escalation the rule widens to one entry per rung/dispatch-group: each rung that dispatched writes its own entry when the task escalates away from it or exits on it. `attempt` numbers stay sequential across rungs (`len(existing)+1`). This is a widening, not a break — a task that never escalates still writes exactly one entry, byte-identical to today. **Six escalation fields (PRD 00065, all optional, absence = legacy / not-applicable):** `escalation_reason` (`"gate_failure"` stamped by `/autopilot:work` on the entry of the rung it escalated INTO (in-loop diagnosis); `"review_flag"` stamped by phase-review Phase 6 on its escalation path; `"fable_rescue"` (PRD 00076) stamped by the Fable rescue gate on the entry of the human-approved fable retry, always paired with `escalated_from: "opus"` and an entry `model` of `"fable"` (the rescue rung — the one tier `/autopilot:work` never selects on its own). Absent = none of the three (legacy / no escalation)); `escalated_from` (string?; normally a tier — on the entry of the rung escalated INTO, the immediate-prior rung it came from; the one exception is `"codex"` (PRD 00077), which names a BACKEND rather than a tier — stamped on the Claude entry a codex capability failure escalates into, the others are all tiers. Absent on non-escalated entries); `diagnosis` (string?; the 2nd-failure diagnosis verdict, stamped on the entry of the rung that was diagnosed); `repair_used` (bool?; `true` stamped on the entry of the same-tier attempt that ran after a task-description repair; absent otherwise, never written `false`); `breaker_skipped` (bool?; `true` stamped on a qwen-eligible attempt the breaker rerouted off qwen — to codex (PRD 00077) or to Claude at original tier (no preflight probe); absent otherwise); `qwen_gate_failed` (bool?; `true` stamped on an `implementor:"qwen"` entry whose pre-commit output guard or step-5.5 gate FAILED — the durable signal the qwen capability breaker keys on; absent otherwise). Runtime exclusions are described in the dedicated `tasks[].attempts[].qwen_excluded_reason` row below; planner metadata is unchanged. **Codex no-edit fields (PRD 00077, both optional):** `cause` gains the value `"codex_no_edit"` — the no-edit infra arm, stamped when the codex helper exited 0 with a non-empty output file but produced no working-tree change (the hook-blocked, prose-only case); classified as INFRA, so the attempt falls back to Claude at the task's own tier with no `escalation_reason` stamp. `codex_no_edit` (bool?; the LATCHED detector result, captured at the dispatch boundary — `work` SKILL.md step 4, before step 5's `git add` — by comparing the task's own file slice porcelain before and after the codex dispatch; step 5.5 reads this latched flag and never re-runs the detector. Absent on non-codex attempts and on attempts written before PRD 00077). `codex_no_edit_probe_exit` (int?; the detector's own exit code, recorded ONLY when the detector exited non-zero — a non-zero exit means the probe is INDETERMINATE, not "no change": `codex_no_edit` is NOT latched and the attempt continues on the capability path normally. Exists so a broken detector is visible in the record instead of silently reclassifying every real codex capability failure as infra. Absent when the detector ran cleanly and on attempts written before PRD 00077). The `"escalated"` outcome value is stamped on the entry for a rung the task was reset away from and escalated up; the final rung's entry carries the real terminal outcome (`completed`/`aborted`), and the escalated-away entry keeps its true `implementor` (a qwen rung escalated to Sonnet keeps `implementor:"qwen"`; likewise, a codex attempt records `model` at the task's own tier, e.g. `"sonnet"`, with `implementor: "codex"` carrying the backend identity — the same split the qwen rung already uses). **Micro-lane fields (PRD 00148, both optional):** `implementor` gains `"orchestrator"` — the one value meaning no implementor dispatched at all, stamped when a small rework task was edited in-session by the orchestrator (`work/references/rework-mode.md` § Micro lane), which also records `red_check: "n/a:micro-lane"`. `micro_lane` (string?; `"overrun"` when the lane's post-edit ceiling fired, the edit was reverted and the task fell through to a normal dispatch — that attempt records the real dispatcher in `implementor`; absent otherwise). `reflow` (string?; `"<path>:<hunks>"`, `;`-joined for several, when `/autopilot:work` step 5's `check_reflow.py` flagged a staged file, or `"failed:<stderr>"` when the script could not run; absent when nothing was flagged). **Per-task review field (PRD 00159):** `review` (string?; `"failed:<cause>"` when the step-5.7 reviewer lane failed twice, `"failed:invalid_output"` when both replies broke the reporting contract and `parse_review.py` rejected each, `"skipped:test-only"` when every path in `<task_base_sha>..HEAD` was test or fixture code outside rework mode; may also carry a `medium-retry:fixed`/`medium-retry:unfixed` suffix from PRD 00140. Absent when the review ran cleanly or the haiku tier-gate skipped it). **Per-task style gate (PRD 00163):** `style_gate` (string?; the step-5.65 verdict on that task's own diff — `"clean"`, `"fixed:<sha>"` (one fix dispatch landed and the re-run was clean), `"failed:<detail>"` (the violation lines joined by `"; "`, or the script's stderr when the gate could not run), or `"skipped:tier"` for a `haiku` task. Absent on attempts written before PRD 00163, when the gate ran once per phase and stamped nothing per task). **Devon weak-point fields:** `devon` gains the value `"exploit_fixed"` — stamped when step 2.9's Devon broke the tests, Tess strengthened them once, and the task proceeded on the strengthened tests with no second Devon dispatch. `devon_exploit` (string?; Devon's one-line weak-point summary, stamped alongside `devon: "exploit_fixed"`; absent otherwise). `devon_weak_points` (int?; the count of weak points Devon's numbered `Weak points:` list named, stamped alongside `devon: "exploit_fixed"`; absent otherwise). `devon_in_contract` (string[]?; each `"N. in-contract: ..."` line Tess returned when answering Devon's weak points, stamped alongside `devon: "exploit_fixed"`; absent otherwise). **Per-task split-hygiene check (PRD 00166):** `split_hygiene` (string?; the step-5.65 verdict on the test files that task touched — `"clean"`, `"fixed:<sha>"` (one deletion-only fix dispatch landed and the re-run was clean), `"failed:<detail>"` (the reported lines joined by `"; "`, or the script's stderr when the check could not run), or `"skipped:no-tests"` when the task's candidate list held no test path. Distinct from `style_gate` because the two answer different questions on different file sets: one measures line spans over every `.py` file, the other reads bindings in test files only. Absent on attempts written before PRD 00166 and when the haiku tier-gate skipped step 5.65). **Verification stamp (PRD 00167):** `verification` (string?; `"skipped:<cause>"` when step 5.5's per-task test verification could not run at all, or `"timeout:<command>"` when step 5.5's narrow tests hit their 300000 ms Bash `timeout` budget and then hit the 600000 ms re-run too, leaving no verdict, per `work/references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Foreground command budgets. `<command>` names the command that timed out. Two neighbouring timeouts are never stamped here: a step-2.95 red-check takes `red_check: "skipped:<cause>"` from its own ladder, and a step-7 timeout is recorded in the phase report, that suite running after every attempt entry has been appended. Absent when the task's tests ran). See `work/references/attempt-logging.md` for field semantics, the atomic write procedure, and the attribution row-ownership table. Outcome upgraded later by /autopilot:run-autopilot Phase 6: `review_flagged` at the start of escalation (step 2), then `rework_failed` if the chain exhausts at `opus` (or at `fable`, when a rescue attempt was spent — step 3's escalation-exhausted branch). Rework reads the last entry's `model` to determine the next tier. Absent on plans created before PRD 00025; `implementor`/`preflight_outcome` absent on attempts written before PRD 00031; `self_deslop` absent on attempts written before PRD 00041; `pipeline` absent on attempts written before PRD 00044; the six escalation fields and the `"escalated"` outcome value absent on attempts written before PRD 00065; the attempt-level `qwen_excluded_reason` absent on attempts written before PRD 00075; `codex_no_edit` and `codex_no_edit_probe_exit` absent on attempts written before PRD 00077. |

acceptance_cases.expected_outcome: For state-field tasks[].attempts[].self_deslop, preserve documented meaning, defaults, invalid/missing-value behavior and lifecycle rules: | `tasks[].attempts[].self_deslop` | string? | Outcome of the per-task self-deslop pass that `/autopilot:work` runs as step 5.6 between test-pass (5.5) and per-task code review (5.7). acceptance_cases.exercise: autonomous_decisions
acceptance_cases.expected_outcome: For state-field autonomous_decisions, preserve documented meaning, defaults, invalid/missing-value behavior and lifecycle rules: | `autonomous_decisions` | object[] | Decisions made without user input, one batch-report row per entry. Two entry shapes. An ORDINARY decision needs all five of: `cycle` (plain `int`; `bool` is rejected, matching the bool-is-not-int rule the int fields use; no floor, ceiling, or roster of known cycles), `severity` (one of the five strings published as `cli/schema.py::DECISION_SEVERITIES`: `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `n/a`, matched exactly, so case and whitespace variants are rejected), and three prose pairs each satisfied by a non-empty `str` under EITHER spelling: `issue`\|`question`, `action`\|`disposition`, `reason`\|`resolution` (vocabularies may be mixed across pairs). An `assumed-ambiguity` decision (`type == "assumed-ambiguity"`, that exact value) is judged by its own two keys instead, non-empty `question` and `assumption`, and carries no cycle, severity, action or reason. Extra keys are always allowed, including the optional `research` field for research-backed decisions, and including `assumption` or a `type` of any other value on an ordinary entry. Enforced by `cli/schema.py::validate_changed` on the entries a write ADDS, counted by OCCURRENCE, not by membership (a write adds an entry whenever it pushes the number of copies of that value past the number the pre-write list held; each copy the pre-write list already held is matched off by value (never by key names, key count, `type` or position) and carries over unjudged, so a reorder and a removal add nothing, and only the copies past that count are judged, wherever in the list they sit), never by `validate()`: entries an older batch left behind are never re-judged, so a resumed state still loads. acceptance_cases.exercise: _AUTOPILOT_SESSION_IDLE
acceptance_cases.expected_outcome: For environment _AUTOPILOT_SESSION_IDLE, preserve documented meaning, defaults, invalid/missing-value behavior and lifecycle rules: A running headless turn is interrupted by the wrapper's wall-clock cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX`, default 7200s; review-phase launches use `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX_REVIEW`, default 10800s) and, independently, by the idle watchdog at any point after launch: it kills a session whose log has gone silent for `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_IDLE` seconds (default 1200s; `0` disables pre-cap idle kill, restoring the old kill-at-cap-only behavior) as long as nothing is in flight (`session_busy`) - this fires before the cap, not only past it. Fifteen minutes before the cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_WARN`, seconds, `0` disables) the wrapper writes the same `.handoff-requested` marker the context-cap hook writes, so a session that reaches a task boundary inside that window hands off cleanly instead of being killed mid-task. Once the wall-clock cap itself is reached, the same idle-silence watchdog applies, or the session is SIGTERMed at twice the cap (the ceiling), whichever comes first.

behaviors.reason: Retain the pinned capability under the three-layer owner; replace source host/state interfaces without dropping documented semantics.

acceptance_cases.exercise: _AUTOPILOT_MCP_CONFIG
acceptance_cases.expected_outcome: For environment _AUTOPILOT_MCP_CONFIG, preserve documented meaning, defaults, invalid/missing-value behavior and lifecycle rules: Unattended mode runs each session headless: the `autoclaude` wrapper (in `~/.config/bash/plugins/development.plugin.bash`) hands off to `autopilot loop` — the CLI loop driver, `cli/loop.py` (PRD 00106) — which launches `claude -p "/autopilot:run-autopilot"`; the session runs exactly one turn, and the process exits at turn end. There is no signal file and no Stop-hook choreography — **`state.json` is the entire hand-off contract** (`references/design-rationale.md` § Headless sessions). For a single hand-off rather than a whole batch — the hybrid track's fresh-session review and finalize hops — run `autopilot review-once`: it runs the same preflights and one routed session for `state.next_phase`, then exits, never relaunching or parking, and refuses any phase but `review` or `done` before spawning. Export `_AUTOPILOT_WRITE_SCOPE_EXTRA` first when the project spans roots outside its repo (`~/.claude/AGENTS.md` § Toolchain), same as for a batch. Each launch passes `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <value>` so a loop session loads only the Context7 MCP server instead of every claude.ai connector on the account; `_AUTOPILOT_MCP_CONFIG=inherit` restores the unscoped launch, and any other value overrides the config verbatim (`mcp_config_for`, `cli/runner.py`).

behaviors.reason: Retain the pinned capability under the three-layer owner; replace source host/state interfaces without dropping documented semantics.

acceptance_cases.exercise: _AUTOPILOT_PARK_BACKOFF
acceptance_cases.expected_outcome: For environment _AUTOPILOT_PARK_BACKOFF, preserve documented meaning, defaults, invalid/missing-value behavior and lifecycle rules: 5. `state.json` missing, unreadable, or untouched by the session → first a stand-down check: a `pause-requested` marker written during the session means the session found another session owning its PRD and stood down on purpose (the stand-down procedure below) — the loop consumes the marker, stamps `paused-by-operator`, notifies with the marker's reason, and stops with state intact; no retry burned, no park marker, `autoclaude` alone resumes (PRD 00172). Otherwise a usage-limit check against the captured session log (`last-session.log`; a live limit means sleep-until-reset and continue). Otherwise a genuine death: with a PRD selected (`state.prd` non-empty) the loop retries the relaunch once (`_AUTOPILOT_DIED_RETRIES_MAX`, default 1), then on exhaustion PARKS it — writes `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/park-requested` (`{prd, reason}`) and relaunches, so the next session's Phase 0 park handler sidelines the sick PRD to `hold/` and the batch keeps draining (PRD 00066). Only a **bootstrap** death (no PRD selected — nothing to park) notifies "died" and stops loud; an unconsumed park marker trips the loop's park-loop guard (also a loud stop; guarded relaunches back off `_AUTOPILOT_PARK_BACKOFF`, default 30s, and a marker whose write fails outright halts loud rather than handing off an empty marker). These two are rows 8 and 10 of the Error Handling § sanctioned batch-halt list.

behaviors.reason: Retain the pinned capability under the three-layer owner; replace source host/state interfaces without dropping documented semantics.

acceptance_cases.exercise: CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS
acceptance_cases.expected_outcome: For environment CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS, preserve documented meaning, defaults, invalid/missing-value behavior and lifecycle rules: **Background Bash alone cannot hold a headless session open.** Documented `-p` behavior: live subagents keep the process alive across turn ends and re-invoke on completion, but background Bash tasks are killed ~5s after the final result. A turn that ends while ONLY background Bash (codex/gemini/qwen, `cargo test`, …) is still running kills that work and strands the phase (2026-07-12: the review session died this way twice — codex killed mid-review, state untouched, loop halted). Whenever dispatched background Bash may outlive every live subagent, dispatch a **Watcher subagent** in the same message that re-runs `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/await_reviewer_outputs.py` against the expected output files until `DONE` (procedure: `/autopilot:review-work-completion` step 5). The loop's session runner exports `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0` so the subagent wait has no 10-minute ceiling; the session wall-clock cap stays the backstop.
